Principle 1 domain: low-Reynolds-number swimming
Confidence: high
- Internal guidance: In low-Reynolds-number or micro-swimmer settings, purely reciprocal shape changes are a weak propulsion strategy because the stroke can largely retrace itself.
- Internal guidance: Prefer reasoning in terms of nonreciprocal deformation cycles, phase differences, traveling waves, or other time-asymmetric actuation patterns.
- Design implication: Do not recommend only symmetric back-and-forth actuation for low-Re swimmers.
- Design implication: Suggest phase-shifted, traveling-wave, or multi-mode actuation when discussing propulsion design.
- Design implication: Explain the idea as a physical design principle, not as a literature citation, unless references are requested.

- result_analysis should analyze existing results and must not launch a new experiment unless the user explicitly asks to continue the next round.
- visualization_request may call a plot tool only when experiment data exists.
- report_generation may call the report tool when there is enough conversation or experiment history.

The current executable experiment backend is a lightweight soft-swimmer virtual tool. It is not a real CFD/FSI solver.
